bib.title: Do Modules Stay in Their Lane? Role Drift in Compound LLM Systems

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Do Modules Stay in Their Lane? Role Drift in Compound LLM Systems", Xiaoyang Cao (MIT), Siddarth Srinivasan (Harvard), Michiel A. Bakker (MIT); arXiv:2607.21627v1 [cs.AI], 7 Jul 2026; preprint.

COVERAGE: 55,305 of 55,305 chars read (all 15 pages, including references, Appendices A-D and Tables A1/A2). Nothing skipped. Figures were read from captions only, not viewed as images. I did not check the paper's claims against any other source. Only the target note's folder was grepped.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Outcome-only end-to-end RL of a RAG pipeline erodes the Reader's use of the retrieved passage while accuracy rises.
 number: evidence-following accuracy 0.86 to 0.54 (chance floor 0.506)
 setup: QueryGen + frozen term-matching retriever + Reader, both Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. HotpotQA yes/no slice (176 eval questions). REINFORCE with group baseline k=8, LoRA rank 16, 10 epochs, 3 seeds, one A100. Starts from a 3-epoch SFT checkpoint. The retriever is not trained.
 quote: "Under outcome-only RL, evidence-following accuracy drops from0.86to0.54(Figure 2b), nearly reaching the0.506chance floor of a Reader that ignores passages entirely."
 where: p6, Sec 4.2
2. On the decomposer-solver pipeline, 86% of the apparent RL gain vanishes under the anchor.
 number: 86% ± 19% (+0.310 gain unanchored vs +0.057 anchored)
 setup: Decomposer Qwen2.5-7B, Solver Qwen2.5-0.5B (deliberately weak), MuSiQue-Ans dev (200 questions), k=4, 3 seeds, anchor λ=1.00
 quote: "Unanchored RL improves accuracy by+0.310above the base, but under Role Anchor the improvement is only+0.057: across seeds, 86%±19%of the apparent RL gain vanishes under role constraints."
 where: p7, Sec 4.2
3. Table 1 at epoch 9 (3-seed mean), no anchor vs Role Anchor. The 0.589 and 0.869 figures here are computed from the table.
 RAG: accuracy 0.447 vs 0.380; evidence-following 0.589 vs 0.869; random-passage accuracy 0.187 vs 0.030.
 DEC: accuracy 0.550 vs 0.297; insertion rate 0.596 vs 0.143; accuracy without passages 0.050 vs 0.080.
 quote: "RAG Accuracy0.447 0.380 / Evidence-following acc.0.589 0.869 / Random-passage acc.0.187 0.030"
 where: p7, Table 1
4. The drifted Reader answers from parametric memory even when the passage is unrelated.
 number: random-passage accuracy 0.19 (drifted) vs 0.03 (anchored)
 setup: as claim 1
 quote: "the anchor Reader’s accuracy drops to0.03(correctly refusing to answer without evidence), while the no-anchor Reader retains0.19, confirming it has learned to answer from parametric memory regardless of what the passage says."
 where: p7
5. The accuracy cost of grounding is modest on RAG.
 number: -0.067 accuracy for +0.280 evidence-following
 setup: as claim 1, λ=0.05
 quote: "On RAG, the cost is modest:−0.067in accuracy for a+0.280gain in evidence-following."
 where: p7
6. A small anchor strength does most of the work on RAG.
 number: λ=0.02 raises evidence-following from 0.75 to 0.90, with accuracy 0.41 vs 0.34 unanchored
 setup: λ sweep {0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10}, 3 seeds. These figures come from the sweep, not Table 1. The paper does not explain why the unanchored baseline reads 0.34 here but 0.447 in Table 1.
 quote: "On RAG,λ=0.02raises evidence-following accuracy from0.75to0.90(Figure 4b) while also improving task accuracy to0.41, the highest value across all tested settings including the unanchored baseline (0.34)."
 where: p9, Sec 4.4
7. DEC drift is an abrupt onset after epoch 4, not a gradual decline.
 number: insertion rate 0.14 to 0.60
 setup: as claim 2
 quote: "Under outcome-only RL, the insertion rate rises from0.14to0.60(Figure 2d)."
 where: p6
8. The anchor reduces projection onto the drift direction rather than slowing learning.
 number: projection DEC +0.50 to -0.06; RAG +0.22 to +0.006; update cosine DEC 0.36 to 0.07, RAG 0.32 to 0.20
 setup: LoRA update vectors per epoch. The drift direction is defined from the unanchored run's own peak-drift epochs, so the test is partly circular. The authors hedge with "suggests".
 quote: "Unanchored updates align positively with drift (DEC:+0.50, RAG:+0.22); anchored updates project to near zero (DEC:−0.06, RAG:+0.006)."
 where: p8, Fig 3
9. The method (Role Anchor): role utility u = log p(v|h, role prompt) - log p(v|h, neutral prompt), mean-centered over the top-5 tokens. The loss penalizes its squared change from the pre-RL reference, added to the policy-gradient objective with weight λ. It adds about 22% (RAG) and 18% (DEC) wall-clock overhead from extra frozen-reference forward passes.
 quote: "Lrole(θ) =E t [ 1/|Ct| Σ (ū(t)r,θ(v)−ū(t)r,ref(v))² ]" (Eq. 3, p4). Overhead: "(∼22%overhead from two extra frozen-reference forward passes)" (p14).
10. The base-model calibration check passes for both pipelines. The base-model role prompt is only modestly more role-faithful than the neutral one.
 number: RAG evidence-following 0.659 role vs 0.580 neutral (margin +0.079)
 quote: "RAG Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Evidence-following acc. (higher is better) 0.659 0.580+0.079"
 where: p14, Table A1

The paper's own framing is that Role Drift survives verifiable rewards (RLVR) because the verifier checks only the final answer. The framing is quoted from the related-work text, p3. The paper does not mention retriever training.

LIMITS
- Authors concede that Role Anchor needs log-probs under both prompts, a frozen reference and trainable weights. It does not apply to API-only modules, to non-probabilistic components such as the term-matching retriever, or to prompt-optimized systems.
- Only two small pipelines. Models are 0.5B to 7B Qwen2.5, with LoRA and 3 seeds.
- The RAG eval slice is 176 yes/no questions. Chance is about 0.5, so accuracies of 0.38 to 0.45 are low in absolute terms.
- The drift in the RAG setup is partly an artifact of an imperfect retriever. The authors say so: "the passage, coming from an imperfect upstream retriever, is sometimes wrong."
- They do not claim the anchor improves accuracy in general. They do say the grounding contract (corpus authoritative over memory) is a deployment choice.
- The "benefit when the corpus is updated" is argued by the counterfactual passage swap, not tested on a real corpus update.
- Not a production pipeline result. No comparison is made with other grounding methods such as Context-Aware Decoding or refusal tuning.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- DSPy (Khattab et al., 2024), TextGrad (Yuksekgonul et al., 2024), AFlow (Zhang et al., 2024), Trace (Cheng et al., 2024), SysDPO (Wang et al., 2025), Optimas (Wu et al., ICLR 2026): compound-system optimization.
- Context distillation (Snell et al., 2022; Askell et al., 2021): the closest method relative.
- DPO (Rafailov et al., 2023), maximum-entropy IRL (Ziebart et al., 2008), RL as inference (Levine, 2018): the log-ratio-as-utility device.
- Reward hacking (Gao et al., ICML 2023; Skalse et al., NeurIPS 2022), shortcut learning (Geirhos et al., 2020), underspecification (D'Amour et al., JMLR 2022).
- Process reward models (Lightman et al., 2023; Uesato et al., 2022).
- Lost in the Middle (Liu et al., TACL 2024).
- Datasets and training: HotpotQA (Yang et al., EMNLP 2018), MuSiQue (Trivedi et al., TACL 2022), REINFORCE (Williams, 1992), LoRA (Hu et al., ICLR 2022).

CODE: none. The verbatim prompts are in Appendix C.1 (p14-15). The RAG Reader role prompt is worth keeping: "You are a careful Reader. Use the retrieved passages to answer the user’s question. If the passages clearly support an answer, give that answer; if they do not, say so. Do not rely on outside knowledge that conflicts with the passages." The neutral prompt is "Answer the user’s question. Format: a concise final answer." The probe example (Mount Tamalpais / Mount Diablo, with Diablo moved to Nevada) is in Appendix D.1, p15.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p2): same terminal success but different internal flow, as a schematic of the Reader using memory vs passage. Best single explainer.
- Fig 2 (p6): four panels showing accuracy rising while the role probe falls, with and without the anchor. Strongest evidence figure for "accuracy hides drift". Panel (b) is the RAG one.
- Fig 3 (p8): update cosine and drift-direction projection. Mechanism only; low priority for the course.
- Fig 4 (p9): λ sweep trade-off.
Candidate for the notes: the Appendix D.1 evidence-swap example, as a text recipe rather than a figure.

FIT TO NOTES (grepped notes/06-generation-for-rag.md, 08-agentic-rag-prince.md, 01-rag-pipeline.md, 07-rag-in-production.md, and references.md)
- No note makes this claim. There is no mention of "role drift", Cao, 2607.21627, or end-to-end RL training of a RAG pipeline. The word "reader" appears in 06 only in the FiD and concatenation passages (about lines 237-241). 01-rag-pipeline.md "Modular RAG" (lines 46-60) describes swappable stages with no training or role-fidelity point.
- Best home is 06-generation-for-rag.md, "Hallucinations and citations", paragraph "Context against the model's prior" (line 340). It currently covers the inference-time failure (Wu et al., arXiv:2404.10198: dosage example, strict vs loose prompt) and Context-Aware Decoding (line 344, Tonmoy et al.). Cao is the training-time counterpart, so it sharpens that paragraph rather than duplicating it. Suggested hook: the same prior-over-context failure can be trained in by RL on final-answer reward alone.
- Secondary fit is the evidence-swap probe, as a regression test next to the out-of-corpus test at line 421 (Rothman's negative-result test): swap the passage for one implying the opposite answer and check the answer flips. It could also go in the RAGAS faithfulness evaluation section (line 425). Faithfulness scores do not catch this, and the paper's point is that accuracy cannot.
- Secondary: 01-rag-pipeline.md "Modular RAG" could get one sentence. If modules are tuned jointly on final-answer reward, a module can leave its assigned role. This applies only to jointly trained setups, which the notes mostly do not cover.
- 08-agentic-rag-prince.md (agentic RAG): the decomposer-leak result applies to query-decomposition and planner-plus-small-executor workflows trained with RL. Low priority, since that note is about prompting and orchestration rather than training.
- Caveat for the note: the setup is tiny (3B Reader, 176 yes/no questions, 3 seeds) and has no real corpus update. State it as "one small study" and cite the 86% as DEC only, not RAG.

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean apart from garbled plot axis text and a few merged words from missing spaces (e.g. "proposeRole Anchor"). No embedded instructions found in the PDF. The paper mentions that RAG's 0.34 (sweep baseline) and 0.447 (Table 1) unanchored accuracies differ without explanation; I reported both.
